data.title: Rocker Nene Royal confident as she heads to AGT finale
data.description: PHUKET - Young rocker Nene Royal will depart this resort island on Tuesday for her last and most important performance in America's Got Talent, as the series reaches its seasonal finale.

data.title: Hong Kongers hit with unauthorised charges for new iPhone as banks launch probes
data.description: Scores of Hong Kongers have complained about unauthorised transactions on credit cards used to pre-order Apple's latest iPhones, prompting major banks to launch investigations.

data.title: Chinese millionaire fugitive arrested in Pattaya, has fake Thai ID
data.description: A Chinese millionaire arrested in Pattaya for illegally acquiring Thai citizenship is also wanted in China for alleged assault three decades ago.

data.title: Okinawa voters elect pro-US base governor
data.description: TOKYO - A candidate backed by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's ruling party won a gubernatorial election in Okinawa, bringing to power a leader who approves of a contentious US military base relocation plan for the first time in 12 years.

data.title: Crowd Erupts as Miss International Queen Reveals Costume Top Three
data.description: Roaring crowds watched 27 nations vie for Best Costume as Miss International Queen 2026 named its Talent Quest winner before Pattaya's grand finale.

data.title: US hosts G20 'energy abundance' talks amid Iran war shock
data.description: HOUSTON, Texas - The United States on Monday kicks off a set of G20 meetings touting "energy abundance," even as President Donald Trump's war against Iran continues to disrupt global fuel markets.

data.title: South Korea aims to save seniors lost in digital age
data.description: SUWON (SOUTH KOREA) - A little cheer rose for 79-year-old Hwang Sun-hee after she managed to place an online order at a training session in South Korea, which has one of the world's starkest digital divides for seniors.

data.title: Taylor's Schools Enters Thailand as St. Andrews International School Joins the Group
data.description: Taylor's Schools, one of Southeast Asia's leading K-12 education groups, today announced the transition of St. Andrews International School, marking the group's entry into Thailand and its ﬁrst expansion beyond Malaysia and Singapore. The transaction comprises four St. Andrews campuses:Sathorn, Dusit, and Sukhumvit 107 in Bangkok, and Green Valley on Thailand's Eastern Seaboard.

data.title: Polls open in Philippine Muslim enclave after deadly shooting
data.description: MARAWI (PHILIPPINES) - Voters across the Philippines' autonomous Muslim region began casting ballots for their first elected parliament Monday morning, hours after gun violence left at least three people dead outside a polling station.

data.title: Migrant workers flock to Indian Kashmir despite militant threats
data.description: SRINAGAR (INDIA) - Every spring, mason Mohammad Ghulam Sarwar boards a train to Indian Kashmir, seeking higher wages despite the risk of being targeted by militants in the disputed Himalayan region.

data.title: Canada's Carney seeks closer Europe ties to counter hostile US
data.description: MONTREAL (CANADA) - Prime Minister Mark Carney calls Canada "the most European of non-European countries," and while formal EU membership may be tricky, he is pursuing unprecedented closeness with the bloc to reduce dependence on a hostile United States.

data.title: Zverev holds off Shelton to win US Open title
data.description: NEW YORK - Alexander Zverev held off Ben Shelton to win the US Open on Sunday, capturing the second Grand Slam of his career just months after winning the French Open.

data.title: Artist Kitti Narod returns  with first solo show in 5 years
data.description: Thai artist Kitti Narod returns to Bangkok for his first solo exhibition in five years, "A Place We Share", at Tang Contemporary Art, until Oct 18.

data.title: Ecocide in focus at 'Negotiating Danger'
data.description: The commodification of natural and human resources is portrayed in "Negotiating Danger: Contemporary Javanese Scrolls", which is running at the Curved Wall, 4th floor of Bangkok Art and Culture Centre, Pathumwan intersection, until Sunday.

data.title: 'Fed up': Thousands march against Sinaloa Cartel violence
data.description: CULIACáN (MEXICO) - Chanting and waving banners, thousands marched Sunday in the Mexican city of Culiacan to protest the deaths of people caught up in a war between two rival factions of the infamous Sinaloa Cartel.

data.title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launched over 50 strikes against them in 24 hours
data.description: SANAA - Yemen's Houthis said Sunday that Saudi Arabia had launched more than 50 strikes against their positions in 24 hours, after the Iran-backed group claimed a rare drone and missile attack on a military base in the kingdom.

data.title: DC's Kennedy Center faces bankruptcy, closure: media
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Leaders of the Kennedy Center who have sought to add President Donald Trump's name to the storied institution say it is facing bankruptcy and possible closure in days, the Washington Post reported Sunday.

data.title: Central's 'Time & Treasures' luxe watch  fest running at Chidlom, Embassy malls
data.description: Central Chidlom and Central Embassy have joined hands to present "Time & Treasures", an exceptional watch and jewellery event that brings together 50 leading brands from around the world until Oct 11.

data.title: Govt clarifies aid to Cambodia
data.description: Government spokesman Ekkapob Pianpises on Sunday denied Thailand had approved a new 31-million-baht aid project for Cambodia, saying the actual allocation is 18.2 million baht to cover interest payments on two previously completed infrastructure projects.
